column11: all of it, because the US infant indication already exists and has since May 2025. The MenQuadfi label (DailyMed setid ab1c3318-578e-4d0c-a21e-fc6df07e9fb7, SPL version 16, effective 2026-04-23) states 'MenQuadfi is approved for use in individuals 6 weeks of age and older', and its Table 1 gives the schedules: '2 months - 4-dose series at 2, 4, 6, and 12 through 18 months of age. The first dose may be given as early as 6 weeks', '6 months through 11 months - 2-dose series with the second dose administered in the second year of life and at least 3 months after the first dose', '12 months through 23 months - 2-dose series with the second dose administered at least 3 months after the first dose'. The FDA approval letter is on file: STN BL 125701/262, 2025-05-23, 'to update the Package Insert to include safety and effectiveness data from postmarketing requirement (PMR) studies MET41, MET42 and MET61 that support lowering the age for use to include individuals 6 weeks through 23 months of age', and 'We note that you have fulfilled the pediatric study requirement for all relevant pediatric age groups for this application.' Sanofi says the same in its Q2 2025 results release (2025-07-31): 'The US FDA updated MenQuadfi's approval to now include active immunization in children aged six weeks to 23 months'. NCT07710872 enrols 2 to 23 months, every one of whom is inside that label
column12: indication_layer.build refuses at 1.0 and should. There is no US readout to wait for: the US paediatric approval happened eighteen months before this catalyst's 2028-03-13 date. THE THING A READER SHOULD TAKE FROM THIS ROW IS NOT THE NUMBER, IT IS THE TWO FACTS UNDER IT. First, NCT07710872 is a CHINA registration study, eight sites all in China, against CanSino's Menhycia, under Chinese schedules; it has nothing to do with a US label. Second, and this is the part that is actually worth money, the US infant opportunity is gated on ACIP and not on licensure. ACIP's controlling document is still MMWR Recomm Rep 2020;69(RR-9):1-41, whose Table 2 for ages '2 mos-10 yrs' reads 'Not routinely recommended' for MenACWY, and CDC's posted child schedule of 2025 (revised 2025-07-02) still gives MenQuadfi a minimum age of '2 years' and, even in Special situations, 'MenQuadfi - Dose 1 at age 24 months or older'. More than a year after the 6-week approval the schedule has not followed it. The catalyst that would move US revenue is an ACIP vote, which data/curated_catalysts.csv is the place for, not this study
